claims.text: The target nanoparticles contain five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios and initially form a single-phase homogeneous solid solution.
Long-term structural and chemical stability is governed by the magnitude of atomic-size-mismatch-induced lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion elevates activation barriers for atomic diffusion.
Lattice distortion elevates activation barriers for elemental segregation.
Above a critical lattice-distortion threshold, nanoparticles will retain a homogeneous solid solution during thermal cycling from 473 to 1923 K.
Lower lattice distortion leads to phase separation and loss of stability during thermal exposure.
Minor deviations from equiatomic composition can be used to produce controlled differences in atomic-size mismatch and lattice distortion.
Local lattice distortion and short-range-order fluctuations mediate the activation energy for atomic diffusion.
Local lattice distortion and short-range-order fluctuations govern the onset of elemental segregation or phase separation.
Large lattice distortions limit thermally activated atomic mobility.
Reduced atomic mobility suppresses nucleation and growth of ordered intermetallic or segregated phases.
Insufficient lattice distortion permits high-temperature diffusion, causing phase instability and chemical degradation.
Higher-distortion nanoparticles will remain single-phase with less segregation and compositional drift from 473 to 1923 K than lower-distortion baseline nanoparticles.
Higher-distortion nanoparticles will retain catalytic and thermoelectric performance better than lower-distortion baseline nanoparticles.
Equiatomic baseline nanoparticles without enhanced lattice distortion are prone to diffusion-driven phase separation and chemical segregation after extended high-temperature exposure.
The proposed mechanism applies when atomic-size effects dominate and oxidation, intrinsic chemical reactivity, and substrate interactions are secondary.
The critical lattice-distortion magnitude is not quantitatively established and may depend on elemental combination and environment.
